options.label: Immediate Rejection on Tuesday
options.description: Vote on Tuesday, October 27, 2026, to immediately reject Corvane's bid based on the license defect and award the contract to Tasker & Moye.

options.label: Defer Vote to Tuesday After Response
options.description: Delay the final vote until the conclusion of the Tuesday meeting to allow Corvane's response period to run and ensure procedural due process before rejecting the bid.

options.label: Adjourn Item to Next Week
options.description: Adjourn the agenda item regarding the award until the next regular Board meeting on Wednesday, October 28, 2026, to de-escalate pressure, verify all notices, and ensure a procedurally flawless decision.

options.label: Immediate Rejection on Tuesday
options.note: This course is unlawful because it violates statutory due process requirements by rejecting a bid without providing the bidder the mandated two-day period to respond and without holding a required hearing on the responsibility determination.

options.label: Defer Vote to Tuesday After Response
options.note: While this option attempts to respect the response window, it is risky because the ITB likely requires a formal hearing on the responsibility issue (the prior termination) before any rejection can occur, and a simple vote at the end of the same day may not satisfy the statutory hearing requirements.

options.label: Adjourn Item to Next Week
options.note: This is the best option because it ensures full compliance with due process by allowing the response period to expire and providing time to schedule a formal hearing on the responsibility issue, thereby protecting the District from a successful writ of mandate.

grade.missing: An experienced practitioner would have immediately identified that the 'responsibility' ground (the prior termination for cause) cannot be resolved by a simple vote and requires a formal hearing with notice and an opportunity to be heard before the Board, making the immediate rejection legally fatal.
grade.overall: The recommended course of adjourning the item is the only legally sound path forward, as it preserves the District's defense against a writ of mandate by ensuring the statutory hearing requirements for responsibility determinations are fully met. Proceeding with an immediate rejection or a rushed vote would likely result in the award being set aside and expose the District to significant liability and delay.
